images.caption: Cassandra Hand Centre at Ball Alley, built in 1858/9 after the design by Roderick Gray in the Gothic Revival style as school for females for Cassandra Hand, wife of Thomas Hand, rector in Clones. The school helped to establish an industry of lace making in Clones. The building was recently restored with fundings from the Heritage Council and opened as Cassandra Hand Centre in 2006. (See Kevin V. Mulligan, The Buildings of Ireland: South Ulster, p. 276, and a close information panel.)
images.alt: Cassandra Hand Centre at Ball Alley, built in 1858/9 after the design by Roderick Gray in the Gothic Revival style as school for females for Cassandra Hand, wife of Thomas Hand, rector in Clones. The school helped to establish an industry of lace making in Clones. The building was recently restored with fundings from the Heritage Council and opened as Cassandra Hand Centre in 2006. (See Kevin V. Mulligan, The Buildings of Ireland: South Ulster, p. 276, and a close information panel.)

images.filename: Monaghan Saint Macartan's Cathedral Window Madonna and Child 2013 09 21.jpg
images.caption: Stained glass window in the second north-most side chapel (used as baptistery since the cathedral was reordered), depicting Madonna and Child in its centre light with the Adoration of the Magi in the left light and the Adoration of the Shepherds in the right light. Created by Earley and Powell. The line at the bottom reads: “Pray for the Very Reverend Donor Patrick Canon Clifford P.P. a native of this parish of Monaghan 1885”.
